newsitem.title: USA: Calif. legislator introduces 10 pct tax cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Calif. legislator introduces 10 pct tax cut plan.

text.p: California state Assembly Republican Leader Curt Pringle on Monday introduced legislation to reduce the state's bank and corporation tax rate by 10 percent over the next two years.
After Pringle introduced the bill, Republican Gov. Pete Wilson issued a statement urging the state legislature to approve the measure.
Wilson proposed the 10 percent bank and corporation tax cut as part of his 1997-1998 budget plan.
"We must continue our efforts to improve the jobs climate in California," Wilson said. "California's competitors are eager to wrestle our companies and jobs away from us."
Last year, 29 states, including five western states, enacted tax reductions. Thirteen states, including California and Washington, enacted some form of a corporate tax cut.
Wilson's tax cut plan has come under fire from some Democrats, who warn the cuts would be a drain on the state budget. Some Democrats are seeking more targeted tax relief.
